first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates that shortening onboarding can improve time-to-value and early adoption. I would verify that evidence and the competing promotional-pricing result because price pressure is immediate, but discounting may reduce sustainable qualified revenue and attract lower-value accounts. A small guarded onboarding test best addresses the current funnel deterioration while limiting downstream revenue risk.

final.rationale: Run a standard, instrumented onboarding-shortening experiment this week. The verified source shows higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and a 3% lift in 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure completion, first meaningful action, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention, preserving uncertainty about how strongly the prior effect transfers to the current cohort.
